{{ElectionsME}}

The '''2026 United States Senate election in Maine''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Maine]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Susan Collins]] is seeking a sixth term. She is being challenged by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former state Senate president [[Troy Jackson]]. The election will be conducted with [[Instant-runoff voting|ranked-choice voting]].

In the June 9 primaries, Collins was the only candidate to qualify for the Republican nomination. Sullivan harbor master [[Graham Platner]] won the Democratic primary over Governor [[Janet Mills]] with the support of progressive leaders, but withdrew from the race on July 10 following sexual assault accusations and other controversies. Jackson was chosen to replace Platner via a [[Party conference#United States|nominating convention]] on July 25.

As Collins is the only Republican senator representing a state that President [[Donald Trump]] did not win in any of his three presidential campaigns, the race is considered to be among the most competitive in 2026. Democrats have not won a Senate election in Maine since [[1988 United States Senate election in Maine|1988]].{{efn|[[Angus King]], who was elected in [[2012 United States Senate election in Maine|2012]] and re-elected in [[2018 United States Senate election in Maine|2018]] and [[2024 United States Senate election in Maine|2024]], is an independent who caucuses with the Democrats, but is not a member of the party.}}

== Background ==
The election will be held on November 3, 2026,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.haaretz.com/us-news/2026-05-04/ty-article/.premium/jewish-groups-withhold-support-as-platner-becomes-maine-frontrunner/0000019d-f412-de15-a7df-f67ba8b30000|title=Jewish Political Groups Withhold Support From Graham Platner After He Emerges as Maine Democratic Frontrunner|website=Haaretz.com|last=Nechin|first=Etan|date=May 4, 2026}}</ref> coinciding with [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Maine|elections]], a [[2026 Maine gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]], and other local elections.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mainepublic.org/tags/your-vote-2026|title=Your Vote 2026|website=Maine Public|access-date=May 8, 2026}}</ref> Both the primary and general elections will be conducted with [[Instant-runoff voting|ranked-choice voting]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Maine elections, 2026 |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Maine_elections,_2026 |website=Ballotpedia |access-date=September 5, 2025}}</ref>
Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. senator [[Susan Collins]] is running for re-election to a sixth term.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mainepublic.org/news/2026-02-10/susan-collins-formalizes-reelection-bid-will-seek-sixth-term|title=Susan Collins formalizes reelection bid, will seek sixth term|first=Steve|last=Mistler|date=February 10, 2026|website=Maine Public}}</ref> Both primary elections took place on June 9, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/polls/maine-us-senate-election-polls-2026.html|title=Maine U.S. Senate Election 2026: Latest Polls|work=The New York Times |date=January 16, 2026|via=NYTimes.com}}</ref>

The northernmost state in [[New England]], [[Maine]] is considered to be a moderately [[Red states and blue states|blue state]]. Maine has voted for every Democratic presidential nominee since [[1992 United States presidential election in Maine|1992]], and Democratic nominee [[Kamala Harris]] defeated Republican nominee [[Donald Trump]] by approximately seven percentage points in the [[2024 United States presidential election in Maine]]. Democrats also control the [[Governor of Maine|governorship]], the [[Maine Legislature|state legislature]], and both seats in Maine's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] [[Maine's congressional delegations|congressional delegation]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cover |first=Susan |title=Maine Democrats say they won enough seats to control state Senate |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/me/maine/politics/2024/11/06/maine-democrats-say-they-won-enough-seats-to-control-state-senate |date=November 6, 2024 |access-date=December 7, 2024 |website=[[Spectrum News#Spectrum News Maine|Spectrum News]] |language=en}}</ref> Since 2018, Collins has been the only Republican representing any New England state in either chamber of Congress.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scanlan|first=Quinn |title=Susan Collins, Congress's last New England Republican, facing toughest reelection yet |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/susan-collins-congresss-england-republican-facing-toughest-reelection/story?id=71716146 |date=July 11, 2020 |access-date=August 1, 2025 |website=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |language=en}}</ref>

Collins was first elected in [[1996 United States Senate election in Maine|1996]]. She has been re-elected in four subsequent elections, significantly outperforming other Republicans in the state. In [[2020 United States Senate election in Maine|2020]], despite almost all polls and analysts predicting that she would lose her re-election bid, Collins defeated Democratic nominee [[Sara Gideon]] by a nine-point margin. Democratic presidential nominee [[Joe Biden]] carried Maine by about nine percentage points on the same ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Everett |first=Burgess |date=November 4, 2020 |title=Collins wins again in Maine, boosting Senate GOP |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2020/11/04/maine-senate-election-results-2020-434000 |access-date=December 7, 2024 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en}}</ref>

This election is expected to be among the most competitive Senate races in 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Sullivan |first1=Andy |last2=Erickson |first2=Bo |date=March 2, 2026 |title=Eight US Senate races to watch in the 2026 midterm elections |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/eight-us-senate-races-watch-2026-midterm-elections-2026-03-02/ |access-date=April 2, 2026 |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> Collins is the only Republican senator who represents one of the 19 states that [[Donald Trump]] did not win in any of his three presidential campaigns.<ref name=CP1>{{Cite web|url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/the-end-of-the-line-for-red-state-senate-democrats/|title=The End of the Line for Red State Senate Democrats|access-date=July 9, 2025|date=December 5, 2024|first1=Kyle|last1=Kondik|website=Sabato's Crystal Ball|quote=Collins is now the lone outlier among all 100 senators as someone who continues to hold a Senate seat in a state that hasn't supported her party's presidential nominee in decades. Such outliers were important parts of past recent Democratic Senate majorities, but they will now be all gone.}}</ref> With the decline of [[Split-ticket voting|ticket splitting]], Collins is widely viewed as the most vulnerable incumbent Republican senator in 2026.<ref>{{cite news |last=Coleman |first=J. Miles |title=The Shocking Decline of Senate Ticket-Splitting |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/articles/the-decline-of-senate-ticket-splitting/ |access-date=April 27, 2023 |work=[[Sabato's Crystal Ball]] |date=July 11, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Newsweek">{{Cite web |last=Stanton |first=Andrew |date=November 14, 2024 |title=Susan Collins' Reelection Plan Throws a Wrench in Democrats' Senate Hopes |url=https://www.newsweek.com/susan-collins-reelection-plans-2026-senate-1986125 |access-date=November 14, 2024 |website=[[Newsweek]]}}</ref> Collins is also the only Republican senator facing re-election in a state that [[Kamala Harris]] won in the [[2024 United States presidential election in Maine|2024 presidential election]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/04/17/jordan-wood-challenge-susan-collins-maine-00297115|title=Democrat eyes challenge to Susan Collins in Maine|date=April 17, 2025|website=Politico|last=Mutnick|first=Ally}}</ref> Since the [[2024 United States Senate elections]], Collins has been the last senator to represent a non-swing state (in other words, a reliably [[Red states and blue states|Democratic or Republican state]]) that typically supports the opposing party.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://rollcall.com/2025/01/08/senate-democrats-personal-brands-midterm-elections/ |title=How the decline of personal political brands hurts Senate Democrats |last=Gonzales |first=Nathan L. |work=[[Roll Call]] |date=January 8, 2025}}</ref>

==Republican primary==
Incumbent U.S. senator [[Susan Collins]] officially announced her re-election bid in February 2026.<ref name="CollinsInterest">{{Cite web |last=Collins |first=Susan |date=February 10, 2026 |title=Susan Collins: I'm running for reelection because experience and independence matter for Maine |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/02/10/opinion/opinion-contributor/susan-collins-reelection-experience-independence-matter/ |access-date=February 10, 2026 |website=Bangor Daily News}}</ref> Despite Collins receiving backlash from some Republicans for not supporting all of Trump's agenda during his [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|second term as president]], the Republican Party nonetheless supports her re-election campaign due to the fact that she is the only Republican who has been electorally successful in Maine in recent years.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kobin |first1=Billy |title=Who will Democrats find to run against Susan Collins in 2026? |url=https://observer-me.com/2025/04/19/news/who-will-democrats-find-to-run-against-susan-collins-in-2026/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250419230724/https://observer-me.com/2025/04/19/news/who-will-democrats-find-to-run-against-susan-collins-in-2026/ |archive-date=April 19, 2025 |date=April 19, 2025 |access-date=April 27, 2025 |website=Piscataquis Observer}}</ref> However, she faced an unsuccessful primary challenge from former police officer Dan Smeriglio, who argued that she votes with [[Senate Democratic Caucus|Senate Democrats]] too often.<ref name="Calabrese">{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Emma |date=June 5, 2025 |title=Eyeing a sixth term, Collins is facing pressure from both sides |url=https://mainemorningstar.com/2025/06/05/eyeing-a-sixth-term-collins-facing-pressure-from-both-sides/ |access-date=September 16, 2025 |website=[[Maine Morning Star]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Smeriglio">{{cite news |last=Collins |first=Steve |date=February 18, 2025 |title=A Frenchville Republican challenges Susan Collins |url=https://www.sunjournal.com/2025/02/18/a-frenchville-republican-challenges-susan-collins/ |access-date=February 19, 2025 |work=[[Sun Journal (Lewiston, Maine)|Sun Journal]]}}</ref> Ultimately, Collins was the only Republican to qualify for the primary ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Pendharkar |first1=Eesha |last2=McCauley |first2=Lauren |date=March 16, 2026 |title=Here's the final list of who is running in Maine's June primary elections |url=https://mainemorningstar.com/2026/03/16/heres-the-final-list-of-who-is-running-in-maines-june-primary-elections/ |access-date=March 17, 2026 |website=Maine Morning Star |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Democratic primary==
In April 2025, former congressional staffer Jordan Wood became the first Democrat to enter the race, running on a platform opposed to the [[Presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] and [[Elon Musk]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cover |first=Susan |date=April 24, 2025 |title=Democrat announces bid to unseat Maine Sen. Susan Collins |url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/me/maine/politics/2025/04/24/democrat-announces-bid-to-unseat-maine-sen--susan-collins |access-date=October 27, 2025 |website=[[Spectrum News]] |language=en}}</ref> 

On August 19, Sullivan harbor master [[Graham Platner]] launched a [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] campaign backed by [[Bernie Sanders]] and organized labor, positioning himself against the "[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic establishment]]" and drawing support from both liberal voters and some [[Donald Trump 2024 presidential campaign|2024 Trump]] voters.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/08/19/graham-platner-maine-senate-campaign-launch-00513884|title=Maine oyster farmer wants to upend Democratic politics with Senate bid|date=August 19, 2025|website=[[Politico]]|last=Otterbein|first=Holly}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Shapiro |first=Lisa Wood |date=September 25, 2025 |title=Can a Maine Oyster Farmer Defeat a Five-Term Republican Senator? |url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/the-political-scene/can-a-maine-oyster-farmer-defeat-a-five-term-republican-senator |access-date=October 9, 2025 |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref> In February 2026, ''Politico'' described Platner as "unlike any other recent popular candidate the state has seen". Noting Platner's large social media following, ''Politico'' added: "He is brash. He is progressive. He has drawn crowds of hundreds of people, national attention and millions in campaign dollars".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/22/maine-senate-graham-platner-janet-mills-susan-collins-00791784|title=Why Graham Platner's meteoric rise is so unexpected|date=February 22, 2026|website=Politico}}</ref>

After weeks of speculation and leaked campaign plans,<ref>{{Cite web |author=Graham, Gillian |date=October 10, 2025 |title=Report: Gov. Janet Mills to launch U.S. Senate campaign on Tuesday |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2025/10/10/report-gov-janet-mills-to-launch-u-s-senate-campaign-on-tuesday/ |access-date=October 10, 2025 |website=[[Portland Press Herald]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Gov. [[Janet Mills]] entered the race in October 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bowman |first=Bridget |date=October 14, 2025 |title=Maine Gov. Janet Mills launches Senate run against one of Democrats' top 2026 targets |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/maine-gov-janet-mills-launches-senate-run-democrats-top-2026-target-rcna233220 |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref> The DSCC's close involvement in her campaign prompted backlash and allegations of favoritism in the primary.<ref>Multiple sources:
* {{Cite web |date=October 15, 2025 |title=Democratic Senate leaders spark fury by backing Janet Mills in Maine |url=https://www.newsweek.com/democratic-senate-leaders-spark-fury-backing-janet-mills-maine-10883646 |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}
* {{Cite web |last=Mistler |first=Steve |date=October 14, 2025 |title=Maine Gov. Janet Mills enters crowded Democratic race to unseat Susan Collins |url=https://www.mainepublic.org/politics/2025-10-14/maine-gov-janet-mills-enters-crowded-democratic-race-to-unseat-susan-collins |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Maine Public |language=en}}
* {{Cite news |last=Newell |first=Jim |date=October 16, 2025 |title=Democrats' Blockbuster Senate Primary Is Set |url=https://slate.com/news-and-politics/2025/10/graham-platner-janet-mills-maine-democratic-senate-primary.html |access-date=November 26, 2025 |work=Slate |language=en-US |issn=1091-2339}}
* {{Cite web |last=McIntire |first=Niels Lesniewski and Mary Ellen |date=October 14, 2025 |title=Maine Gov. Janet Mills enters Senate race against Susan Collins |url=https://rollcall.com/2025/10/14/maine-gov-janet-mills-officially-enters-senate-race/ |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Roll Call |language=en-US}}
</ref><ref name="pt">{{Cite web |last=Kondik |first=J. Miles Coleman and Kyle |date=October 16, 2025 |title=Maine Senate Primary Tests Whether Democrats Will Keep Deferring to Their Leaders |url=https://centerforpolitics.org/crystalball/maine-senate-primary-tests-whether-democrats-will-keep-deferring-to-their-leaders/ |access-date=November 26, 2025 |website=Sabato's Crystal Ball |language=en-US}}</ref> Mills was widely viewed as a top Democratic recruit; she was encouraged to run by [[Party leaders of the United States Senate|Senate Minority Leader]] [[Chuck Schumer]], Senator [[Kirsten Gillibrand]], and the [[Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee]] (DSCC),<ref>Multiple sources:
* {{Cite web |last=Neukam |first=Stephen |date=September 9, 2025 |title=Senate Democrats locked in 2026 proxy war |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/09/09/schumer-bernie-sanders-2026-senate-primary-races |access-date=October 15, 2025 |website=Axios |language=en}}
* {{Cite web |last=Andrews |first=Ethan |date=September 10, 2025 |title=Janet Mills is interviewing staff for a potential Senate run |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2025/09/10/politics/washington/janet-mills-is-interviewing-staff-for-a-potential-senate-run/ |access-date=October 9, 2025 |website=Bangor Daily News |language=en-US}}
* {{Cite web |last1=Nichols |first1=Hans |last2=Neukam |first2=Stephen |date=September 19, 2025 |title=Scoop: Gov. Janet Mills "likely" to run for Senate to try to defeat Susan Collins |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/09/19/janet-mills-maine-senate-2026 |access-date=October 9, 2025 |website=Axios |language=en}}
* {{Cite web |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/10/14/janet-mills-enters-crowded-maine-senate-race-00597876 |title=Chuck Schumer gets his preferred candidate, Janet Mills, in crowded Maine Senate race |date=October 14, 2025 |website=Politico}}</ref> although Sanders publicly discouraged her candidacy.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Parks |first=Molly |date=October 9, 2025 |title=Sanders publicly discourages Janet Mills run for Maine Senate seat |url=https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/congressional/3844631/bernie-sanders-publicly-discourages-janet-mills-maine-senate-campaign-2026/ |access-date=October 10, 2025 |work=Washington Examiner |language=en-US}}</ref> 

Following Mills's entry, several candidates, including Dan Kleban and Daira Smith-Rodriguez, withdrew and endorsed Mills.<ref name="KlebanWithdrawal">{{Cite web |last=Kobin |first=Billy |date=October 14, 2025 |title=Maine Beer Co. leader Dan Kleban leaves Senate race to endorse Janet Mills |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2025/10/14/politics/elections/dan-kleban-leaves-senate-race-endorse-janet-mills/ |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[Bangor Daily News]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="RodriguezWithdrawal">{{Cite tweet |number=1981450170756690050 |user=DairaForME |title=Today, I am formally suspending my campaign. I want to thank my team, our volunteers, and everyone who supported our fight. I look forward to continuing to fight alongside Maine activists as we work to protect our communities in these trying times. |date=October 23, 2025}}</ref> Smith-Rodriguez cited concerns over past comments by Platner regarding sexual assault in the military.<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web |last1=Mancini |first1=Ryan |title=Maine Senate candidate drops out, citing Platner's post on military rape |work=The Hill |date=October 24, 2025 |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5572083-maine-senate-candidate-dropout-graham-platner-comments/ |access-date=February 2, 2026}}</ref> Wood later withdrew to run for the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]].<ref name=wgme>{{cite web |last1=St Pierre |first1=Ariana |title=Senate candidate Jordan Wood drops out to run for Maine's 2nd District seat |url=https://wgme.com/news/local/senate-candidate-jordan-wood-drops-out-to-run-for-maines-2nd-district-seat-susan-collins-paul-lepage-jared-golden-politics |access-date=November 12, 2025 |work=[[WGME]]|language=en |date=November 12, 2025}}</ref>

In January 2026, Platner briefly paused his campaign due to his wife's medical treatment abroad<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 11, 2026|title=Graham Platner to take campaign hiatus to travel to Norway for IVF with wife|url=https://www.newscentermaine.com/article/news/local/graham-platner-to-take-campaign-hiatus-to-travel-to-norway-for-ivf-with-wife/97-6efaee11-e76f-41fe-9d3d-6259b56221c0|access-date=January 12, 2026|website=newscentermaine.com|language=en-US}}</ref> before resuming later that month. He returned to the campaign trail with protests against [[Immigrations and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE) enforcement actions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Platner calls Collins' ICE announcement 'pinky promise'|url=https://spectrumlocalnews.com/me/maine/politics/2026/01/29/protesters-rally-with-graham-platner-to-demand-end-to-ice-funding|access-date=February 10, 2026|website=spectrumlocalnews.com|language=en}}</ref>

In February 2026, Mills committed to multiple debates ahead of the June 9 primary.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Davis |first=Emma |date=February 24, 2026 |title=Mills announces series of Democratic debates in lead up to U.S. Senate primary |url=https://mainemorningstar.com/briefs/mills-announces-series-of-democratic-debates-in-lead-up-to-u-s-senate-primary/ |access-date=February 24, 2026 |website=Maine Morning Star |language=en-US}}</ref>

Mills, Platner, and [[2024 United States Senate election in Maine|2024 nominee]] David Costello qualified for the primary ballot.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kail |first=Benjamin |date=March 16, 2026 |title=A 3rd Democrat joins Janet Mills and Graham Platner in Maine's US Senate primary |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/03/16/politics/elections/david-costello-maine-democratic-us-senate-candidate/ |access-date=March 17, 2026 |website=Bangor Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> In addition, [[University of Maine]] adjunct professor Andrea LaFlamme started a write-in bid for the Democratic nomination.<ref name=":1" />

The Platner/Mills contest was seen as a key contest between the Democratic Party's [[Centrism|centrist]] establishment wing and the [[Populism in the United States|populist]] [[Left-wing politics|left-wing]] and [[Progressivism in the United States|progressive]] faction, with Mills representing the former and Platner representing the latter.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 30, 2026 |title=Graham Platner surge threatens Susan Collins as Janet Mills bows out |url=https://www.newsweek.com/graham-platner-threatens-susan-collins-janet-mills-maine-senate-11898302 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref> 

In March 2026, Mills began running [[attack ad]]s highlighting Platner's controversies. By April 2026, multiple polls had been released which showed Mills as much as 38 points behind Platner in the primary.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leading in Primary by 38 Points, Platner Takes Aim at Collins' Wall Street Cash and Iran War Support|work= Common Dreams |url=https://www.commondreams.org/news/graham-platner-vs-susan-collins |access-date=April 9, 2026 |language=en}}</ref> Shortly thereafter, the Mills campaign stopped running the attack ads and had made no additional ad purchases across any platform, leading to rumors that she would withdraw from the race.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=April 8, 2026 |title=Janet Mills drops attack ads, but is still 'full steam ahead' in US Senate primary |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2026/04/08/janet-mills-drops-attack-ads-but-is-still-full-steam-ahead-in-us-senate-primary/ |access-date=April 9, 2026 |website=The Portland Press Herald |language=en-US}}</ref> 

On April 30, Mills announced that she was suspending her campaign, but she did not endorse him. Her withdrawal led to Schumer and Gillibrand announcing they would now help Platner to defeat Susan Collins.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 30, 2026 |title=Maine Gov. Janet Mills suspends Senate campaign |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/maine-gov-janet-mills-suspends-senate-campaign-rcna342859 |access-date=April 30, 2026 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref>

Following the end of Mills' campaign, Platner was the only prominent and competitive Democrat left in the race, making him the most likely Democratic nominee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 30, 2026 |last1=Mueller |first1=Julia |last2=Parnes |first2=Amie |title=Democrats coalesce around Platner as Mills exits Maine Senate race |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5858298-democrats-rally-around-platner-maine-senate-mills-exit/ |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=The Hill |language=en-US}}</ref> Mills' name remained on the primary ballot,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kail |first=Benjamin |date=May 5, 2026 |title=Janet Mills hasn't formally exited Maine's Democratic US Senate primary |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/05/05/politics/elections/janet-mills-hasnt-exited-democratic-us-senate-primary-n6hjn1me0n/ |access-date=May 11, 2026 |website=Bangor Daily News |language=en-US}}</ref> and Costello also continued his campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bishop |first=Bonnie |date=May 6, 2026 |title=Maine Democrat David Costello makes his second bid for US Senate |url=https://www.wmtw.com/article/david-costello-maine-senate-candidate-democrat/71152917 |access-date=May 11, 2026 |website=[[WMTW (TV)|WMTW]] |language=en}}</ref> On June 9, Platner won the primary;<ref>{{cite web |title=Maine U.S. Senate primary results |url=https://apnews.com/projects/elections-2026/maine-primary-results-us-senate/#Dem |website=AP News |publisher=Associated Press |access-date=June 10, 2026}}</ref> he received over 150,000 votes, more than any other Democratic candidate in a primary in Maine's history.<ref>{{cite web |title=Graham Platner gets more primary votes than any other Democratic Senate candidate in Maine history |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/06/11/politics/elections/maine-senate-primary-graham-platner-votes-democratic-history/ |last=Mistler |first=Steve |website=[[Bangor Daily News]] |date=June 11, 2026 |access-date=July 11, 2026}}</ref>

=== Platner misconduct controversies ===
Shortly after Mills entered the race, Platner came under fire for resurfaced controversial [[Reddit]] posts criticizing police officers, calling rural Americans "stupid" and referring to himself as a "communist", resulting in his campaign's political director, former state representative [[Genevieve McDonald]], quitting the campaign and calling Platner "unelectable"; however, [[Democratic National Committee]] Chair [[Ken Martin]] stated that the comments were not disqualifying,<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 19, 2025 |title=DNC Chair Ken Martin says Maine Senate candidate's Reddit posts are 'hurtful' but not disqualifying |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/dnc-chair-ken-martin-platner-maine-senate-reddit-disqualifying-rcna238451 |access-date=October 23, 2025 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref> and Platner apologized in a five-minute video posted to social media. On October 21, Platner released a video of himself dancing and singing shirtless at his brother's wedding, revealing he had a chest tattoo that resembled the ''[[Totenkopf]]'' used by [[Nazi Germany]]'s ''[[Schutzstaffel]]''. Platner stated he got the tattoo while inebriated with other [[U.S. Marines]] while stationed in [[Croatia]], mistaking the symbol for a generic [[skull and crossbones]]. He had the [[Cover-up tattoo|tattoo covered]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reed |first=Russ |date=October 23, 2025 |title=Maine Senate candidate Platner says he's covered up tattoo resembling Nazi symbol |url=https://www.wmtw.com/article/graham-platner-tattoo-covered-up-nazi-totenkopf-skull/69123653 |access-date=October 23, 2025 |website=[[WMTW (TV)|WMTW]] |language=en}}</ref> and professed his shame and disgust for getting a tattoo that resembled the fascist insignia.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Weir |first=Keziah |date=October 23, 2025 |title=Graham Platner—and His Mom—Try to Move Past Tattoo Scandal at a Maine Town Hall |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/story/graham-platner-and-his-mom-try-to-move-past-tattoo-scandal-at-a-maine-town-hall |access-date=October 23, 2025 |magazine=Vanity Fair |language=en-US}}</ref> Platner also called himself an anti-fascist "[[supersoldier]]" in an old Reddit comment.<ref>{{Cite web |first1=Holly |last1=Otterbein |first2=Alex |last2=Thompson |date=October 21, 2025 |title=Maine Dem Senate candidate embraced 'antifa supersoldier' label |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/10/21/maine-democrats-senate-graham-platner-antifa |access-date=October 28, 2025 |website=Axios |language=en}}</ref> After the controversies, Democrats such as Senator [[Chris Murphy]] defended Platner and said that he "sounds like a human being" who is honest about his mistakes.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9o8vE0Js_VE|title='He Sounds Like A Human Being To Me': Chris Murphy Responds To Maine Senate Candidate's Nazi Tattoo|date=October 26, 2025|last=Forbes Breaking News|access-date=November 26, 2025|via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kassel|first=Matthew|date=October 27, 2025|title=Graham Platner's credibility under fire in Maine Senate campaign|url=https://jewishinsider.com/2025/10/graham-platner-democrat-senate-maine-campaign-nazi-tattoo/|access-date=November 26, 2025|website=Jewish Insider|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=Popat/> Senator [[Ruben Gallego]] called his campaign "authentic" and said that he has "the right to grow out of his stupidity" and is not going to be a "crypto-[[John Fetterman|Fetterman]]".<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 8, 2025|title=Graham Platner says he's no John Fetterman. But he gets the concerns.|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/graham-platner-says-no-john-fetterman-gets-concerns-rcna242667|access-date=November 26, 2025|website=NBC News|language=en}}</ref><ref name=Popat>{{Cite news |last=Popat|first=Shrai|date=November 3, 2025|title='In this 'til the end': Maine Senate hopeful Graham Platner on refusing to quit amid furor over 'Nazi' tattoo|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/nov/03/graham-platner-democrat-senate-maine|access-date=November 26, 2025|work=The Guardian|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

On February 26, 2026, Platner quote-tweeted a clip from Donald Trump's [[2026 State of the Union Address]], criticizing Trump's speech. The clip had been posted by anti-Semitic white supremacist [[Stew Peters]].<ref name="MediaiteTweet">{{cite web |last1=Griffing |first1=Alex |title=Progressive Senate Candidate Graham Platner Deletes Tweet Boosting Notorious Neo-Nazi |url=https://www.mediaite.com/media/news/progressive-senate-candidate-graham-platner-deletes-tweet-boosting-notorious-neo-nazi/ |website=Mediaite |access-date=February 28, 2026 |language=en |date=February 26, 2026}}</ref> The tweet was deleted hours later, with a spokesperson for Platner's campaign telling ''[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]'' that they were unaware of Peters's views.<ref name="hilltweet">{{cite web |last1=Fields |first1=Ashleigh |title=Platner deletes social media post promoting far-right figure Stew Peters |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5757567-platner-stew-peters-post-controversy/ |website=The Hill |access-date=February 28, 2026 |date=February 26, 2026}}</ref><ref name="portlandtweet">{{cite web |title=Graham Platner once again under fire for a now-deleted social media post |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2026/02/26/graham-platner-under-fire-for-a-now-deleted-social-media-post/ |website=The Portland Press Herald |access-date=February 28, 2026 |date=February 27, 2026}}</ref>

In May 2026, reports surfaced that Platner's wife had alerted his campaign team to explicit messages he was sending to women on the messaging app [[Kik (app)|Kik]], expressing concern that the behavior could hurt him politically. Additional reports during the same period drew attention to Platner's Nazi-linked tattoos, as well as past social media posts widely described as bigoted.<ref>{{Cite news |title=An increasingly risky bet for Democrats in Maine |url=https://www.economist.com/united-states/2026/06/01/an-increasingly-risky-bet-for-democrats-in-maine |access-date=June 3, 2026 |newspaper=The Economist |issn=0013-0613}}</ref>

In June 2026, ''The New York Times'' published an article including allegations of physical abuse and "unsettling" behavior from multiple women.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Glueck |first1=Katie |last2=Lerer |first2=Lisa |date=June 4, 2026 |title=Several Women Who Dated Graham Platner Recall 'Unsettling' Behavior |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/04/us/politics/platner-maine-senate-girlfriends-relationships.html |access-date=June 10, 2026 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In response, Platner told media that his poor behavior was attributed to PTSD from his service in the Marine Corps. While he specifically denied the accusations made by one woman, he did not dispute the characterization of his behavior toward a second one.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whittle |first=Patrick |date=June 5, 2026 |title=Graham Platner denies an ex-girlfriend's report that he once twisted her arm, held her in a room |url=https://www.wbur.org/news/2026/06/05/graham-platner-ex-girlfriend-allegations-senate-campaign-maine |access-date=June 10, 2026 |publisher=WBUR|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

=== Platner's withdrawal ===
On July 6, 2026, a woman Platner had previously dated accused him of [[rape|raping]] her while he was drunk nearly five years prior.<ref name="Politico SA">{{cite web |last1=Piper |first1=Jessica |last2=Wren |first2=Adam |title=Exclusive: Woman who dated Graham Platner says he sexually assaulted her |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/06/graham-platner-sexual-assault-allegation-00987737 |website=Politico |access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Newsweek SA">{{cite news|date=July 6, 2026|title=Graham Platner facing voter concerns as new sexual assault allegation lands|newspaper=Newsweek|url=https://www.newsweek.com/graham-platner-polls-scandal-susan-collins-12162790|access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Tapper |first1=Jake |last2=Gordon |first2=Allison |title=Woman alleges Graham Platner raped her in 2021 while they were dating, which he denies |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/06/us/graham-platner-racicot-allegation-maine-invs |website=CNN |date=July 6, 2026 |access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref> Platner denied the accusation, accusing it of being a political attack to derail his campaign.<ref name="Politico SA"/><ref name="Newsweek SA"/> The next day, another former girlfriend alleged that he would [[stealthing|take condoms off during sex without her consent]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Brittain |first1=Amy |last2=Goodwin |first2=Liz |last3=Wang |first3=Amy |title=Ex-girlfriend of Graham Platner says he removed condoms without consent during sex |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/07/07/ex-girlfriend-graham-platner-says-he-removed-condoms-without-consent/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=July 7, 2026 |access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Marcus |first1=Josh |title=Graham Platner accuser levels 'stealthing' claim against embattled Maine Senate candidate: report |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/graham-platner-sexual-assault-allegation-b3010812.html |website=The Independent |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref>

Shortly after the rape allegation, U.S. Senator [[Ruben Gallego]] and U.S. Representative [[Ro Khanna]] rescinded their endorsements of Platner,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Howard |first1=Andrew |title=Khanna and Gallego withdraw Platner endorsements |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/06/ro-khanna-ruben-gallego-graham-platner-endorsement-00988368 |website=Politico|access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref> and the [[Maine Democratic Party]] released a statement calling on Platner to suspend his campaign.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Merica |first1=Dan |last2=Koseff |first2=Alexei |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Top Democrats pull Graham Platner endorsements, call on him to end Maine Senate campaign |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/07/06/top-democrats-pull-graham-platner-endorsements-call-him-end-maine-senate-campaign/ |access-date=July 9, 2026 |newspaper=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> Platner later stated on the same day that the campaign would "tak[e] the time to reflect on the best path forward," fueling speculation that he would withdraw from the race.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Downs |first1=Garrett |last2=Papp |first2=Justin |title=Platner Senate campaign taking 'time to reflect' on path forward after sexual assault allegation |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/06/graham-platner-maine-senate-allegation-response.html |website=CNBC |date=July 6, 2026 |access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref> Soon, numerous organizations and U.S. senators, including those who had endorsed Platner, called on him to exit the race.<ref name=PoliticoCallsToDropOut/><ref>{{Cite news|last=Thorp |first=Frank V |date=July 7, 2026 |title=With Sanders dropping his endorsements, Platner has no more Senate backers |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/live-blog/trump-nato-summit-turkey-live-updates-rcna353169/rcrd116253 |access-date=July 8, 2026 |work=[[NBC News]] |language=en}}</ref> Senate Democratic Leader [[Chuck Schumer]] and [[Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee]] chair [[Kirsten Gillibrand]], who also rescinded their endorsements, stated that the DSCC would not invest in the race as long as Platner remained on the ballot.<ref name=PoliticoCallsToDropOut>{{Cite web |last1=Pellish |first1=Aaron |last2=Steakin |first2=Will |last3=Kashinsky |first3=Lisa |last4=Hernandez |first4=Alec |title=Democratic leaders have abandoned Graham Platner |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/06/democrats-abandon-graham-platner-endorsements-support-00988421 |work=[[Politico]] |language=en-US |issn=0098-8421 |date=July 6, 2026 |access-date=July 9, 2026 |archive-date=July 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260707012328/https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/06/democrats-abandon-graham-platner-endorsements-support-00988421 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Statement from Maine Democratic Party Leadership on Allegations Against Graham Platner |url=https://mainedems.org/statement-from-maine-democratic-party-leadership-on-allegations-against-graham-platner/ |website=Maine Democratic Party |date=July 6, 2026 |access-date=July 6, 2026}}</ref><ref name="KruesiRiccardiAP">{{cite news |last1=Kruesi |first1=Kimberlee |last2=Riccardi |first2=Nicholas |title=Democrats begin pulling Platner endorsements after Maine candidate faces sexual assault allegation |url=https://apnews.com/article/graham-platner-maine-assault-senate-061e18bdd180928bbcd94b18a52f4ec9 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=July 6, 2026 |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> On July 8, Platner announced that he would drop out of the race,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kruesi|first1=Kimberlee |last2=Kinnard |first2=Meg |title=Graham Platner says he'll withdraw from Senate race in Maine|url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/graham-platner-says-hell-withdraw-from-senate-race-in-maine |agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=[[PBS News]] |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref> filing his withdrawal two days later.<ref name="WithdrawalReceived"/>

== Democratic nominating convention ==
=== Process ===
No political party in Maine had replaced their nominee in any prior election. While the exact process to be used was not immediately certain, Maine Democratic Party officials and others like [[Maine Senate]] president [[Mattie Daughtry]] called for an open and inclusive process.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mundry |first1=Jackie |title=How does the state Democratic party choose a new candidate? |url=https://www.wmtw.com/article/how-does-maine-democratic-party-choose-new-candidate/71857778 |website=[[WMTW (TV)|WMTW]] |date=July 7, 2026 |access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref> On July 8, the Maine Democratic Party voted to hold a state [[Party conference#United States|party convention]] to nominate a candidate to replace Platner as the Democratic nominee.<ref name="ConDetailsBangor" /> The convention was held on July 25 in [[Bangor, Maine|Bangor]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Democrats in Maine formally nominate Troy Jackson as their new candidate for U.S. Senate|url=https://www.npr.org/2026/07/25/nx-s1-5902982/democrats-maine-senate-race|website=[[NPR]] |access-date=July 25, 2026|date=July 25, 2026|last=Moore|first=Elena}}</ref> In order to qualify for the convention, replacement candidates had until July 15 to declare their intent to run; they also had until July 21 to collect at least 500 signatures, with at least 50 signatures from eight different counties.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Mistler |first1=Steve|last2=Catalina|first2=Andrew |date=July 11, 2026 |title=Maine Democrats outline process for nominating Graham Platner's replacement  |url=https://www.mainepublic.org/politics/2026-07-10/the-latest-on-how-maine-democrats-will-nominate-graham-platners-replacement |access-date=July 25, 2026 |website=[[Maine Public]] |language=en}}</ref> The convention consisted of 601 delegates overall, including the party's state committee.<ref name="ConDetailsBangor">{{Cite news |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/07/08/politics/elections/maine-democrats-want-convention-replace-graham-platner/ |title=Maine Democrats approve 600-person convention to pick Graham Platner's replacement |last=Shepherd |first=Michael |work=[[Bangor Daily News]] |date=July 8, 2026 |access-date=July 9, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://mainemorningstar.com/2026/07/10/heres-what-we-know-about-maine-democrats-plan-to-replace-graham-platner/ |title=Here's what we know about Maine Democrats' plan to replace Graham Platner |last1=Davis |first1=Emma |last2=Pendharkar |first2=Eesha |work=[[Maine Morning Star]] |date=July 10, 2026 |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> 500 of the delegates were elected via county-level [[Caucus#Caucuses to select election candidates|caucuses]] held on July 18–19.<ref name="slates">{{Cite news |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/07/18/politics/elections/everything-to-know-maine-senate-caucuses/ |title=Everything to know about this weekend's chaotic Maine Senate caucuses |last=Shepherd |first=Michael |work=[[Bangor Daily News]] |date=July 18, 2026 |access-date=July 18, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/07/18/us/politics/graham-platner-replacement-democrats.html |title=How Maine Democrats Intend to Replace Graham Platner in 19 Days |last=Wu |first=Ashley |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=July 18, 2026 |access-date=July 18, 2026}}</ref> All delegates at the convention were officially unpledged,<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/10/graham-platner-replacement-scramble-00992699 |title='No one planned for this': The rapidly-evolving 18-day primary to replace Platner |last1=Hernandez |first1=Alec|last2=Howard |first2=Andrew |last3=Piper|first3=Jessica |last4=Doherty|first4=Erin |work=[[Politico]] |date=July 10, 2026 |access-date=July 10, 2026}}</ref> though candidates published slates of committed supporters before the county meetings.<ref name="slates" />

=== Campaign and convention ===
Leading up to and following Platner's withdrawal, former gubernatorial candidates [[Nirav D. Shah|Nirav Shah]], [[Troy Jackson]], and [[Shenna Bellows]] were viewed as likely frontrunners for the replacement nomination.<ref name="KruesiRiccardiAP"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Epstein |first1=Reid J. |date=July 6, 2026 |title=Who Might Replace Platner if He Drops Out? Here's What Could Happen. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/06/us/politics/who-would-replace-graham-platner-maine.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |access-date=July 19, 2026 |quote=They include Ms. Bellows, Troy Jackson, a former president of the Maine Senate, and Nirav Shah, a former director of Maine's public health agency.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Piper |first1=Jessica |last2=Howard |first2=Andrew |date=July 15, 2026 |title=Maine Democrats grapple with who is best to take over Graham Platner's movement |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/15/maine-democrats-fractures-platner-replacement-00997729 |work=[[Politico]] |language=en-US |access-date=July 19, 2026 |quote=The trio of former gubernatorial candidates are the leading figures in a crowded field aiming to win over a yet-to-be-selected group of 600 Democratic delegates.}}</ref> Jackson was the first to declare his candidacy for the Senate nomination,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sopher |first1=Ittai |last2=Park |first2=Jane |date=July 9, 2026 |title=Two Democrats enter race to replace Graham Platner on the ballot in Maine |url=https://www.kgw.com/article/news/nation-world/graham-platner-troy-jackson-maine/507-fee98287-0c78-4ca6-8c4d-cf91637b2720 |work=[[News Center Maine]] |language=en-US |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> while Shah was the first candidate to receive sufficient signatures to qualify.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nirav Shah becomes first candidate to collects required signatures for Senate bid |url=https://wgme.com/news/local/nirav-shah-becomes-first-candidate-to-qualify-for-senate-race-democrats-defeat-susan-collins-tour-senate-maine-hannah-pingree-graham-platner |website=[[WGME-TV|WGME]] |language=en-US |date=July 13, 2026 |access-date=July 13, 2026}}</ref> Following the county meetings, at least 456 of the selected delegates were pledged supporters of Jackson,{{efn|There is inconsistency between reports of the exact number of delegates that pledged for Jackson. The ''[[Bangor Daily News]]'', in their breakdown of county meeting results, reported 456 Jackson delegates.<ref name="BangorDelegateResults"/> ''[[Maine Morning Star]]'' reported 478 Jackson delegates.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://mainemorningstar.com/2026/07/20/heres-how-many-delegates-jackson-won-in-each-county/ |title=Here's how many delegates Jackson won in each county |last=Pendharkar |first=Eesha |work=[[Maine Morning Star]] |date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref> Jackson's campaign gave a figure of 481 delegates.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nbcboston.com/news/politics/troy-jackson-secures-overwhelming-support-to-be-maines-democratic-senate-nominee/3984430/ |title=Troy Jackson secures overwhelming support to be Maine's Democratic Senate nominee |last=Prichard |first=Matt |work=[[NBC10 Boston]] |date=July 20, 2026 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref>}} placing him in the lead for the nomination.<ref name="BangorDelegateResults">{{Cite news |last=Shepherd |first=Michael |date=July 13, 2026 |title=Troy Jackson closes in on Maine's Democratic Senate nod after dominant caucus day |url=https://www.bangordailynews.com/2026/07/18/politics/elections/troy-jackson-dominates-day-1-maine-democratic-senate-caucus/ |work=[[Bangor Daily News]] |language=en-US |access-date=July 20, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Svitek |first1=Patrick |last2=Cohen |first2=Ethan |date=July 18, 2026 |title=Troy Jackson, a former Graham Platner ally, well-positioned to win Maine Democrats' nomination to face Sen. Susan Collins |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/18/politics/troy-jackson-graham-platner-maine |website=[[CNN]] |language=en-US |access-date=July 18, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Pellish & Howard 2026">{{cite news |last1=Pellish |first1=Aaron |last2=Howard |first2=Andrew |date=July 19, 2026 |title=Troy Jackson has effectively secured the Maine Senate Democratic nomination |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/19/troy-jackson-likely-maine-senate-nominee-platner-01004490 |website=Politico |language=en-US |access-date=July 19, 2026}}</ref> Bellows and Shah, along with candidates Dan Kleban and Jordan Wood, all withdrew from the race on July 19.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Wagner |first1=Bayliss |last2=Cromwell |first2=Sydney |last3=Balk |first3=Tim |title=In Maine Senate Race, Jackson Sprints Ahead of Pack, as Bellows Drops Out |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/19/us/politics/maine-senate-bellows-jackson-platner-democrats.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |date=July 19, 2026 |access-date=July 20, 2026 |quote=On Sunday afternoon, Dr. Nirav Shah{{nbsp}}... said he was suspending campaign operations and endorsing Mr. Jackson. Hours earlier, Shenna Bellows{{nbsp}}... ended her Senate campaign. Dan Kleban{{nbsp}}... also dropped out on Sunday evening{{nbsp}}... the last of the four leading candidates, Jordan Wood, also suspended his campaign and said he would back Mr. Jackson.}}</ref>

Jackson and healthcare executive Saundra Pelletier were the only candidates to qualify for the convention ballot and continue their campaigns after the county caucuses.<ref name="2CandidatesWBUR">{{Cite web |title=Competition for Maine's Democratic Senate nomination down to 2 candidates |url=https://www.wbur.org/news/2026/07/23/maine-primary-democrats |last=Miller |first=Kevin |website=[[WBUR-FM|WBUR]] |language=en |date=July 23, 2026 |access-date=July 25, 2026}}</ref> Jackson won the convention vote over Pelletier, 566–5.<ref name="ConvResultUsaToday"/>

===Debates===
A debate featuring eight of the declared candidates, hosted by [[News Center Maine]], occurred on July 16, 2026.<ref name="ReplaceDebate"/> A second debate, hosted by the ''[[Bangor Daily News]]'' and [[CNN]], was scheduled for July 23, but was later cancelled.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Wright |first1=David |title=CNN and Bangor Daily News cancel Maine Senate debate as Democrats rally behind Troy Jackson |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/07/16/politics/cnn-bangor-daily-news-maine-debate |work=[[CNN]] |access-date=July 20, 2026|language=en |date=July 20, 2026}}</ref>
